pathway.title: Brightstar Lottery PLC — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Net leverage is acceptable on management's measure but weaker on a cash-oriented one. Net debt was USD 3,796 million at June 30, 2026 against last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,170 million, which is 3.24x, and total debt over the same EBITDA is 3.72x [financial base: leverage]. Adjusted EBITDA adds back USD 323 million of license-fee amortization for the same period, and without that add-back net leverage is 4.48x [financial base: definition review]. The add-back relates to fees already paid in cash, which is why the reported figure is not unreasonable, but it means the leverage ratio flatters the cash burden of renewals in a business whose Italian licenses run for about nine years. The headline rise from 2.44x at December 31, 2025 to 3.24x mostly reflects the settlement of a USD 1,680 million regulator payable that sat outside debt; counting that payable, leverage at December 31, 2025 would have been 3.94x, so the like-for-like movement over six months was a decrease, helped by USD 650 million of partner capital contributions [financial base: claims outside debt; business context: Italian Lotto license].

Liquidity and maturities are comfortable for two years and heavier after that. Liquidity is USD 1,742 million, made of USD 558 million of cash and USD 1,185 million of undrawn revolver, against 2027 and 2028 principal maturities of USD 1,026 million combined, which is 1.70x cover [financial base: liquidity and maturities]. Total principal is USD 4,383 million, of which USD 2,883 million is in euros and all of it is senior secured, and the 2028 to 2030 maturities total USD 2,801 million, about 64% of principal. The new revolver runs to March 2031 with USD 604 million drawn. The risk is a concentrated refinancing window in 2028 to 2030 that coincides with the Scratch and Win renewal.

Cash generation is positive before license payments but is shared. Operating cash flow excluding Lotto payments was USD 761 million over the last twelve months and free cash flow excluding them USD 387 million; reported free cash flow was negative USD 2,214 million because of the USD 2,601 million of license payments in the period [financial base: financials]. Out of the USD 387 million, partners took USD 163 million of distributions, leaving USD 224 million for debt reduction and shareholders, and shareholder returns of USD 1,090 million over the same twelve months (including the USD 600 million special dividend funded from the sale of the gaming business) therefore came from sale proceeds and not from recurring cash flow [business context: ownership and governance]. In the first half of 2026 free cash flow excluding Lotto payments of USD 269 million less partner distributions of USD 163 million was USD 106 million, below the USD 130 million returned to shareholders. Capital expenditure of USD 190 million is expected in the second half of 2026 for new contracts.

The business has strong contractual visibility, concentrated in Italy and exposed to renewals. About 92% of revenue comes from long-term contracts, but the two Italian licenses supplied about 37% of FY2025 revenue and many U.S. contracts can be ended at will with limited notice [business context: operating model]. The Italian Lotto license runs to November 2034, while the Scratch and Win license expires in September 2028 and is not renewable unless its terms say so; the new Lotto license required an upfront fee of EUR 2,230 million. If a renewal needs a comparable upfront payment, it would arrive when USD 798 million of debt matures, a mechanic and not a forecast, since the renewal terms are not in the evidence.

Partners and the controlling shareholder claim part of the cash flow. The Italian Lotto manager is 61.5% owned by the company's Italian subsidiary, partners contributed USD 650 million of capital in the first half of 2026, and in FY2025 income attributable to non-controlling interests of USD 136 million exceeded total income from continuing operations of USD 135 million [business context: operating model]. De Agostini holds 46.29% of the shares and 63.28% of the votes, so distribution and leverage policy is its to set; the term loan agreements limited distributions at December 31, 2025, but the March 2026 amendment is not supplied.

What is not known matters. Covenant levels are not supplied, so headroom under the maximum net leverage and minimum interest coverage tests cannot be calculated even though the company reports compliance; nothing after August 4, 2026 is available; and ratings are known only at December 31, 2025 (BBB- from Fitch, Ba1 from Moody's, BB+ from S&P) [readiness; financial base: covenants].

runs.text: Strength: contracted, wager-linked revenue. About 92% of FY2025 revenue comes from long-term operating, facilities management and lottery management contracts with a revenue-weighted remaining term of 5.1 years for facilities management contracts and 5.6 years for the Italian licenses, so revenue is visible, and the company owns the technology and equipment it places, including more than 350,000 point-of-sale devices [business context: operating model]. Category: Documentary Fact.

Strength: liquidity and a staggered maturity profile. Liquidity of USD 1,742 million and no maturity before 2027 give two years of room, and the 2027 maturity of USD 228 million is small against that liquidity [financial base: liquidity and maturities]. Category: Documentary Fact.

Strength: deleveraging since the sale of the gaming business. Carrying debt fell from USD 5,361 million at December 31, 2024 to USD 4,178 million at December 31, 2025 and net leverage on management's measure from 4.08x to 2.44x before the Lotto payment, with refinancing already completed for 2026 [financial base: leverage; business context: transactions]. Category: Documentary Fact.
Strength: interest cover. Adjusted EBITDA covers cash interest 6.09x over the last twelve months, against 5.26x in FY2025 [financial base: interest cover]. Category: Analyst Interpretation.

Weakness: leverage quality. Net leverage of 3.24x depends on management's measure that adds back USD 323 million of license amortization; without it leverage is 4.48x and cash interest cover is 4.41x [financial base: definition review]. Category: Analyst Interpretation.

Weakness: Italian concentration and the 2028 renewal. The two Italian licenses are about 37% of revenue, the Scratch and Win license expires in September 2028, and the license assets pass to the State free of charge at expiry [business context: operating model]. Category: Documentary Fact.

Weakness: partner leakage and consolidated figures. Consolidated debt and EBITDA include 100% of the Italian joint venture while partners hold 38.5% of the Lotto manager and non-controlling interests took USD 163 million of distributions in the first half of 2026, so consolidated leverage does not isolate the claims of the parent's creditors on partner-owned cash [business context: operating model]. Category: Analyst Interpretation.

Weakness: customer and jackpot exposure. The top ten customers outside Italy supplied about 35% of FY2025 revenue, a customer that contributed USD 37 million of FY2025 revenue left in August 2025, and lottery management incentives fell by USD 51 million in FY2025 on weak jackpot activity [business context: operating model]. Category: Documentary Fact.

Weakness: control and distributions. One holder controls the vote, shareholder returns have exceeded recurring free cash flow after partners, and creditor protection depends on distribution caps whose current text is not supplied [business context: ownership and governance]. Category: Analyst Interpretation.

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: Sale of the gaming and digital business. On July 1, 2025 the company completed the sale of IGT Gaming to a holding company owned by funds managed by affiliates of Apollo Global Management, pursuant to agreements entered into on July 26, 2024. The 20-F records total consideration, net of $134 million of cash and restricted cash transferred, of $4.1 billion and a pre-tax gain of $112 million (20-F page:156). The business is a discontinued operation, so every continuing-operations comparative excludes it. Continuing involvement is limited to licensing between the two groups, a 60.0% interest in Rhode Island VLT Company LLC whose economic benefits were transferred to IGT Gaming, and a guarantee of a lease of IGT Gaming that expires September 30, 2032 with maximum base-rent exposure of $94 million at June 30, 2026 (Q2 6-K page:17 and page:18). A receivable from the buyer of $21 million at June 30, 2026 will be collected through 2027 (Q2 6-K page:17). De Agostini retained an investment in the combined private company (20-F page:156); its size is not stated in the text read.

Use of proceeds. The filings state two uses. First, debt repayment: on the sale the company redeemed the 4.125% dollar notes due April 2026 and the 3.500% euro notes due June 2026 and prepaid euro term loan and revolver amounts, and the interim notes say $2 billion of debt was required to be repaid within six months of closing (20-F page:170; Q2 6-K page:17). Second, shareholder returns: the 20-F describes a "previously announced plan to return $1.1 billion of net cash proceeds from the IGT Gaming divestiture to shareholders" (20-F page:58). Execution documented in FY2025 includes a special dividend of $600 million (Q4 deck page:6, management claim), a $250 million accelerated share repurchase and a total of $770 million of cash dividends and $271 million of repurchases for the year (20-F page:123 and page:139).

Italian Lotto license. On July 16, 2025 the regulator notified that the consortium led by Brightstar had been awarded the Italian Lotto license for nine years from December 1, 2025. The upfront fee was €2,230 million, paid as €500 million on July 17, 2025, €300 million on November 28, 2025 and €1,430 million ($1,675 million) on April 24, 2026 (20-F page:163; Q2 6-K page:12). The Q1 deck states Brightstar's share of the final installment as €879 million or $1.03 billion (Q1 deck page:6, management claim); that share equals about 61.5% of €1,430 million, consistent with the stated ownership of Lottoitalia. Partners funded their share through non-controlling interest capital increases of $650 million in the first half of 2026 (Q2 6-K page:5). The license is amortized against revenue from December 2025 and the Q2 deck states that about $175 million of incremental Lotto-related service revenue amortization affects FY2026 reported growth (Q2 deck page:7, management claim).

New debt issues and refinancing. In September 2024 Brightstar Lottery Holdings B.V. issued €500 million of 4.250% notes at par (20-F page:170). In March 2025 the Parent and Brightstar Lottery S.p.A. entered into a facilities agreement for two €500 million term loans due September 2030, one used to repay revolver borrowings and one to fund the share of the Lotto fee (20-F page:171). In December 2025 the Parent and a subsidiary as co-issuers issued $750 million of 5.750% senior secured notes due January 2033 at par and used the proceeds and cash to redeem the $750 million 6.250% notes due January 2027 at 101.22%, with a $10 million loss on extinguishment (20-F page:169 and page:170). In March 2026 the company signed new senior secured revolving credit facilities of $650 million and €1.0 billion expiring March 2031, effective April 2026, cancelled both revolvers due July 2027 and amended the 2030 term loans to align provisions; in April 2026 it prepaid the remaining €200 million of the January 2027 term loan from revolver borrowings (Q2 6-K page:15). The June 30, 2026 principal is $4,383 million with the first maturity of $228 million in 2027 (see the financial base). Documented status of all items above: completed. No debt issuance is documented after June 30, 2026.

Subsequent events to the latest report: a dividend of $0.23 per share declared July 30, 2026, repurchases of $10 million to July 31, 2026, and the July 10, 2026 payment of a Mexican tax settlement (Q2 6-K page:17, page:18, page:19). Nothing after August 4, 2026 is supplied.

fields.value: The effective source set supports the requested work with limitations, so every selected consumer is assessed as ready with limitations and none as conditional or blocked. The assertion is source sufficiency only. Whether the later modules accept their inputs is not evaluated here. The audited annual report and the three interim reports give the statements, debt note, maturity table, liquidity table and commitments needed for a financial data build. The business and transaction work has the annual report's business description and the interim notes on the sale of the gaming business and the Italian Lotto license. The principal restrictions are the absence of any report after the August 2026 interim filing, the absence of covenant levels and debt documents, and the reliance on slide decks for Adjusted EBITDA and leverage.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Issuer and reporting entity: Brightstar Lottery PLC (the "Parent") with its consolidated subsidiaries. The annual report states "In July 2025, the Parent changed its corporate name from International Game Technology PLC to Brightstar Lottery PLC (NYSE: BRSL)" (20-F page:4). The pack file names still carry "igt", which is the earlier name, and identity rests on the text, not the filename.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Basis: US GAAP, single operating segment. The interim report states "The Company operates and manages its continuing operations business as a single segment" (second-quarter 2026 interim report page:10).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Perimeter change: the gaming and digital business was sold on July 1, 2025 and is shown as discontinued operations ("On July 1, 2025, the Company completed the sale of the Gaming & Digital business", interim report page:7). Continuing-operations figures for 2025 comparatives therefore exclude that business, and discontinued-operations amounts are separate lines. The annual report, the 2025 nine-month report and the 2026 reports must not be mixed without the discontinued-operations label.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Non-controlling interests: the Italian Lotto license is held through a consortium that Brightstar leads ("a consortium comprised of Allwyn, Arianna 2001, Novomatic Italia, and led by Brightstar", interim report page:12). The income statement and equity statement show non-controlling interests ("Non-controlling interests 1,173 715", interim report page:4), so consolidated cash, debt and EBITDA include partner interests. The ownership percentage of the consortium is not located in the filing text; the Q1 2026 deck gives "BRSL share €879M or $1.03B" of the final installment (Q1 deck page:6), which is a management claim.

fields.value: - Debt roles: the annual report's debt note lists issuers as Parent, Brightstar Lottery Holdings B.V. and "Parent/Brightstar Global Solutions Corporation" for the 2033 notes (20-F page:169). The paragraph below the table names the co-issuer "Brightstar Lottery Global Solutions Corporation". These two spellings are a naming conflict inside one source and need one resolution downstream. Term loan borrower: Brightstar Lottery S.p.A. (20-F page:171). Guarantors are described only as "certain of the Parent’s subsidiaries"; no list of named guarantors is in the pack. Restricted and unrestricted group distinctions are not described in the supplied text.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The financial base is complete enough for the downstream credit work, with three restrictions. First, the reported picture is a company that has just paid a very large one-off cash item: the final Italian Lotto license installment of $1,675 million in April 2026, which turned six-month operating cash flow to a $1,174 million outflow and lifted net debt from $2,732 million to $3,796 million between December 31, 2025 and June 30, 2026. Net debt leverage on management's definition moved from 2.44x to 3.24x, and the December 2025 figure sat beside a $1,680 million payable to the Italian regulator that was outside debt. Second, the leverage and cover ratios rest on Adjusted EBITDA, a management non-GAAP measure that adds back amortization of upfront license fees, and the filings supply no covenant thresholds against which to judge headroom. Third, the capital structure is mainly senior secured, mixed in currency, with about two thirds of principal in euros, and cash distributions to non-controlling interests are a recurring claim on consolidated cash flow. Liquidity of $1,742 million and a first maturity of $228 million in 2027 give near-term room, but the evidence ends at the August 4, 2026 interim report.

fields.value: By currency at June 30, 2026, principal is 1,500 dollar-denominated and 2,883 euro-denominated, together 4,383 (Q2 6-K page:14, "Total principal amounts 1,500 2,883 4,383"). The December 31, 2025 principal of the January 2027 term loan is 235 long-term plus 118 current. Notes are secured by "the shares of Brightstar Lottery S.p.A., certain intercompany loans with principal balances in excess of $10 million, and certain accounts receivable" (20-F page:169). The Q2 6-K says the revolver obligations are guaranteed "subject to agreed guarantor coverage thresholds based on consolidated assets and adjusted EBITDA" (Q2 6-K page:15); the guarantors are not named. Debt is described as all senior secured; no unsecured or subordinated debt, and no structurally separate unrestricted group, appears in the debt note.

fields.value: The revolver agreement "contains a maximum net leverage ratio covenant and a minimum interest coverage ratio covenant" (Q2 6-K page:15) and the borrowers "were in compliance with such covenants" at June 30, 2026 (Q2 6-K page:27). No threshold, step-down, covenant EBITDA definition or reported covenant ratio is printed, so headroom is Not calculable. The term loan agreements at December 31, 2025 limited dividends and share repurchases to "$400 million if any two" ratings are below Ba1/BB+ and $550 million if two are at or above that level, with the cap removed if two ratings are at or above Baa3/BBB- (20-F page:171); the ratings at that date were BBB- (Fitch), Ba1 (Moody's) and BB+ (S&P) (20-F page:168). In March 2026 the company amended certain provisions of the 2030 term loans "to align such provisions under the RCF Agreement" (Q2 6-K page:15) and the amended text is not supplied, so the current distribution cap cannot be stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is a contracted, wager-linked lottery services company whose creditor-relevant features sit in four places. First, revenue visibility is high on paper, with about 92% of FY2025 revenue from long-term operating, facilities management and lottery management contracts, but U.S. contracts can be ended by the lottery authority at will with limited notice and the two Italian licenses together supplied about 37% of revenue. Second, the Italian licenses are the key transaction exposure: the new nine-year Lotto license cost an upfront fee of €2,230 million, paid in three installments ending April 24, 2026, and it is now amortized against revenue; the Scratch and Win license expires in September 2028. Third, control is concentrated in De Agostini with 63.28% of votes, and the documented behaviour since the sale of the gaming business on July 1, 2025 is debt reduction alongside large shareholder distributions, within term loan limits whose current text is not supplied. Fourth, the Italian Lotto structure shares cash flow with partners, so consolidated figures include cash that belongs partly to non-controlling interests. The evidence is adequate for a business-context fact pack, but the concession terms, the consortium agreements and any event after August 4, 2026 are not in the pack.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sale of the gaming and digital business. On July 1, 2025 the company completed the sale of IGT Gaming to a holding company owned by funds managed by affiliates of Apollo Global Management, pursuant to agreements entered into on July 26, 2024. The 20-F records total consideration, net of $134 million of cash and restricted cash transferred, of $4.1 billion and a pre-tax gain of $112 million (20-F page:156). The business is a discontinued operation, so every continuing-operations comparative excludes it. Continuing involvement is limited to licensing between the two groups, a 60.0% interest in Rhode Island VLT Company LLC whose economic benefits were transferred to IGT Gaming, and a guarantee of a lease of IGT Gaming that expires September 30, 2032 with maximum base-rent exposure of $94 million at June 30, 2026 (Q2 6-K page:17 and page:18). A receivable from the buyer of $21 million at June 30, 2026 will be collected through 2027 (Q2 6-K page:17). De Agostini retained an investment in the combined private company (20-F page:156); its size is not stated in the text read.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Use of proceeds. The filings state two uses. First, debt repayment: on the sale the company redeemed the 4.125% dollar notes due April 2026 and the 3.500% euro notes due June 2026 and prepaid euro term loan and revolver amounts, and the interim notes say $2 billion of debt was required to be repaid within six months of closing (20-F page:170; Q2 6-K page:17). Second, shareholder returns: the 20-F describes a "previously announced plan to return $1.1 billion of net cash proceeds from the IGT Gaming divestiture to shareholders" (20-F page:58). Execution documented in FY2025 includes a special dividend of $600 million (Q4 deck page:6, management claim), a $250 million accelerated share repurchase and a total of $770 million of cash dividends and $271 million of repurchases for the year (20-F page:123 and page:139).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Italian Lotto license. On July 16, 2025 the regulator notified that the consortium led by Brightstar had been awarded the Italian Lotto license for nine years from December 1, 2025. The upfront fee was €2,230 million, paid as €500 million on July 17, 2025, €300 million on November 28, 2025 and €1,430 million ($1,675 million) on April 24, 2026 (20-F page:163; Q2 6-K page:12). The Q1 deck states Brightstar's share of the final installment as €879 million or $1.03 billion (Q1 deck page:6, management claim); that share equals about 61.5% of €1,430 million, consistent with the stated ownership of Lottoitalia. Partners funded their share through non-controlling interest capital increases of $650 million in the first half of 2026 (Q2 6-K page:5). The license is amortized against revenue from December 2025 and the Q2 deck states that about $175 million of incremental Lotto-related service revenue amortization affects FY2026 reported growth (Q2 deck page:7, management claim).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: New debt issues and refinancing. In September 2024 Brightstar Lottery Holdings B.V. issued €500 million of 4.250% notes at par (20-F page:170). In March 2025 the Parent and Brightstar Lottery S.p.A. entered into a facilities agreement for two €500 million term loans due September 2030, one used to repay revolver borrowings and one to fund the share of the Lotto fee (20-F page:171). In December 2025 the Parent and a subsidiary as co-issuers issued $750 million of 5.750% senior secured notes due January 2033 at par and used the proceeds and cash to redeem the $750 million 6.250% notes due January 2027 at 101.22%, with a $10 million loss on extinguishment (20-F page:169 and page:170). In March 2026 the company signed new senior secured revolving credit facilities of $650 million and €1.0 billion expiring March 2031, effective April 2026, cancelled both revolvers due July 2027 and amended the 2030 term loans to align provisions; in April 2026 it prepaid the remaining €200 million of the January 2027 term loan from revolver borrowings (Q2 6-K page:15). The June 30, 2026 principal is $4,383 million with the first maturity of $228 million in 2027 (see the financial base). Documented status of all items above: completed. No debt issuance is documented after June 30, 2026.

fields.value: Fundamental credit synthesis for Brightstar Lottery PLC, as of 2026-11-05, pathway credit snapshot. Scope: business risk from the business and transaction handoff and financial risk and liquidity from the financial base handoff, in USD. The latest evidence is the interim report signed August 4, 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: This module works from upstream handoffs only and read no source text directly; the issuer sources below reach it through those handoffs, whose locators are in the earlier modules.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Brightstar Lottery PLC has an adequate fundamental credit profile with real near-term support but limited margin for error. The strongest support is contracted, wager-linked revenue, about 92% of FY2025 revenue, and liquidity of USD 1,742 million with no debt maturing before 2027, after the final USD 1,675 million Italian Lotto payment was absorbed. The weakest point is the quality of 3.24x net leverage: it uses management's Adjusted EBITDA, which adds back USD 323 million of license amortization and would read 4.48x without it, while partners and a controlling shareholder take part of the cash flow. The outcome depends on free cash flow after the investment cycle, the Scratch and Win renewal in September 2028 beside USD 798 million of 2028 maturities, and covenant terms that are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net leverage is acceptable on management's measure but weaker on a cash-oriented one. Net debt was USD 3,796 million at June 30, 2026 against last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,170 million, which is 3.24x, and total debt over the same EBITDA is 3.72x [financial base: leverage]. Adjusted EBITDA adds back USD 323 million of license-fee amortization for the same period, and without that add-back net leverage is 4.48x [financial base: definition review]. The add-back relates to fees already paid in cash, which is why the reported figure is not unreasonable, but it means the leverage ratio flatters the cash burden of renewals in a business whose Italian licenses run for about nine years. The headline rise from 2.44x at December 31, 2025 to 3.24x mostly reflects the settlement of a USD 1,680 million regulator payable that sat outside debt; counting that payable, leverage at December 31, 2025 would have been 3.94x, so the like-for-like movement over six months was a decrease, helped by USD 650 million of partner capital contributions [financial base: claims outside debt; business context: Italian Lotto license].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity and maturities are comfortable for two years and heavier after that. Liquidity is USD 1,742 million, made of USD 558 million of cash and USD 1,185 million of undrawn revolver, against 2027 and 2028 principal maturities of USD 1,026 million combined, which is 1.70x cover [financial base: liquidity and maturities]. Total principal is USD 4,383 million, of which USD 2,883 million is in euros and all of it is senior secured, and the 2028 to 2030 maturities total USD 2,801 million, about 64% of principal. The new revolver runs to March 2031 with USD 604 million drawn. The risk is a concentrated refinancing window in 2028 to 2030 that coincides with the Scratch and Win renewal.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash generation is positive before license payments but is shared. Operating cash flow excluding Lotto payments was USD 761 million over the last twelve months and free cash flow excluding them USD 387 million; reported free cash flow was negative USD 2,214 million because of the USD 2,601 million of license payments in the period [financial base: financials]. Out of the USD 387 million, partners took USD 163 million of distributions, leaving USD 224 million for debt reduction and shareholders, and shareholder returns of USD 1,090 million over the same twelve months (including the USD 600 million special dividend funded from the sale of the gaming business) therefore came from sale proceeds and not from recurring cash flow [business context: ownership and governance]. In the first half of 2026 free cash flow excluding Lotto payments of USD 269 million less partner distributions of USD 163 million was USD 106 million, below the USD 130 million returned to shareholders. Capital expenditure of USD 190 million is expected in the second half of 2026 for new contracts.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business has strong contractual visibility, concentrated in Italy and exposed to renewals. About 92% of revenue comes from long-term contracts, but the two Italian licenses supplied about 37% of FY2025 revenue and many U.S. contracts can be ended at will with limited notice [business context: operating model]. The Italian Lotto license runs to November 2034, while the Scratch and Win license expires in September 2028 and is not renewable unless its terms say so; the new Lotto license required an upfront fee of EUR 2,230 million. If a renewal needs a comparable upfront payment, it would arrive when USD 798 million of debt matures, a mechanic and not a forecast, since the renewal terms are not in the evidence.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Partners and the controlling shareholder claim part of the cash flow. The Italian Lotto manager is 61.5% owned by the company's Italian subsidiary, partners contributed USD 650 million of capital in the first half of 2026, and in FY2025 income attributable to non-controlling interests of USD 136 million exceeded total income from continuing operations of USD 135 million [business context: operating model]. De Agostini holds 46.29% of the shares and 63.28% of the votes, so distribution and leverage policy is its to set; the term loan agreements limited distributions at December 31, 2025, but the March 2026 amendment is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: What is not known matters. Covenant levels are not supplied, so headroom under the maximum net leverage and minimum interest coverage tests cannot be calculated even though the company reports compliance; nothing after August 4, 2026 is available; and ratings are known only at December 31, 2025 (BBB- from Fitch, Ba1 from Moody's, BB+ from S&P) [readiness; financial base: covenants].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength: contracted, wager-linked revenue. About 92% of FY2025 revenue comes from long-term operating, facilities management and lottery management contracts with a revenue-weighted remaining term of 5.1 years for facilities management contracts and 5.6 years for the Italian licenses, so revenue is visible, and the company owns the technology and equipment it places, including more than 350,000 point-of-sale devices [business context: operating model]. Category: Documentary Fact.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength: liquidity and a staggered maturity profile. Liquidity of USD 1,742 million and no maturity before 2027 give two years of room, and the 2027 maturity of USD 228 million is small against that liquidity [financial base: liquidity and maturities]. Category: Documentary Fact.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength: deleveraging since the sale of the gaming business. Carrying debt fell from USD 5,361 million at December 31, 2024 to USD 4,178 million at December 31, 2025 and net leverage on management's measure from 4.08x to 2.44x before the Lotto payment, with refinancing already completed for 2026 [financial base: leverage; business context: transactions]. Category: Documentary Fact.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength: interest cover. Adjusted EBITDA covers cash interest 6.09x over the last twelve months, against 5.26x in FY2025 [financial base: interest cover]. Category: Analyst Interpretation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness: leverage quality. Net leverage of 3.24x depends on management's measure that adds back USD 323 million of license amortization; without it leverage is 4.48x and cash interest cover is 4.41x [financial base: definition review]. Category: Analyst Interpretation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness: Italian concentration and the 2028 renewal. The two Italian licenses are about 37% of revenue, the Scratch and Win license expires in September 2028, and the license assets pass to the State free of charge at expiry [business context: operating model]. Category: Documentary Fact.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness: partner leakage and consolidated figures. Consolidated debt and EBITDA include 100% of the Italian joint venture while partners hold 38.5% of the Lotto manager and non-controlling interests took USD 163 million of distributions in the first half of 2026, so consolidated leverage does not isolate the claims of the parent's creditors on partner-owned cash [business context: operating model]. Category: Analyst Interpretation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness: customer and jackpot exposure. The top ten customers outside Italy supplied about 35% of FY2025 revenue, a customer that contributed USD 37 million of FY2025 revenue left in August 2025, and lottery management incentives fell by USD 51 million in FY2025 on weak jackpot activity [business context: operating model]. Category: Documentary Fact.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness: control and distributions. One holder controls the vote, shareholder returns have exceeded recurring free cash flow after partners, and creditor protection depends on distribution caps whose current text is not supplied [business context: ownership and governance]. Category: Analyst Interpretation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Brightstar's contracted lottery revenue and USD 1,742 million of liquidity support an adequate credit profile, but leverage quality, Italian renewal risk and partner and shareholder claims on cash flow limit headroom until the 2028 to 2030 refinancing window is addressed. Category: Analyst Interpretation.
